title: 10 Best Visily Alternatives in 2026
summary: Visily set October 31, 2026, as its shutdown date. Compare 10 Visily alternatives that import your files, turn screenshots into editable designs or start fresh.
body_markdown:
Key takeaways:


- Visily's own shutdown post set October 31, 2026, as its closing date and says all user data will be permanently deleted on November 30, 2026.
- Five of the nine tools after ours turn a screenshot into an editable design: UX Pilot, Uizard and Banani on their free plans, Balsamiq on every plan (it has no free one) and Mockflow from Plus.
- UX Pilot is the only alternative we found that documents importing Visily's own .vis files, board links and pasted screens.
- Visily's free plan only exported watermarked 1x images and PDFs, so if your boards no longer open, you'll need a screenshot converter to get editable screens back.


Visily, the AI wireframing tool pitched at people who aren't designers, announced it would shut down on October 31, 2026, so the first question to ask of Visily alternatives is whether they can take your old screens back.


This list is for the people Visily was built for: product managers, founders and marketers who mock up screens to explain an idea to a client or a boss.[Awesomic](https://www.awesomic.com/) is first because it's our product. Next comes the one alternative here that imports Visily's own files, then the tools that turn a screenshot into an editable design, then the ones that don't.


Inside each group, the cheapest paid plan billed annually goes first (for the converters, the cheapest one that includes conversion), and the monthly price breaks a tie. We opened every vendor's pricing page on November 13, 2026, and took Visily's last prices from an archived copy of its pricing page.


## What happened to Visily


Visily gave four weeks' notice. Here's the timeline, from Visily's own post and what its website returns now:


- October 3, 2026: the Visily Team publishes "Visily is shutting down" and asks users to "save or export any work you want to keep."
- October 31, 2026: the shutdown date Visily announced.
- By November 6, 2026: archive captures show visily.ai's homepage redirecting to a login screen at app.visily.ai, which today offers sign-in but no sign-up.
- November 30, 2026: Visily permanently deletes all user data.


The post gives one reason: "the market for tools like Visily has changed substantially in the last couple of years." Visily's help center is still online, and its export article confirms that Figma export was "a paid feature".


### What to do before November 30


With sign-up gone, we couldn't test whether existing users can still open boards or export after October 31, so read these steps as "if you can still sign in":


1. Open your most important board first.
2. On a paid plan, use Export to Figma, which saves a .vis file, and keep it even if you never open Figma.
3. On the free plan, try Export to Figma first, since Visily said every design could be exported; if that fails, export each screen as an image or PDF.
4. If exports fail but boards still open, screenshot every screen at full size.
5. Bring .vis files or board links into UX Pilot, or feed the images to a screenshot converter below.


Move fast on that last step. UX Pilot's migration page warns that board links and copy-paste "can stop working at any time", and that images inside .vis files imported after November 30 "may no longer load".


After that date, you start from whatever files you saved, and the real question is how much of the rebuild your new[product design software](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/product-design-software) does for you.


## What Visily users are really replacing


Visily's homepage said it "helps non-designers quickly convey product ideas to clients and executives". You could start a screen from a text prompt, a template, a diagram or a screenshot, switch between low and high fidelity, and comment on boards as a team, with 50 workspace members even on the free plan.


That free plan is the part that matters now. Starter cost $0 for 2 editable boards and 300 AI credits a month, but its exports were JPG, PNG or PDF, "1x only, With watermark". Figma export and Export to Code sat on Pro, listed at $14 "Per editor/month" with no billing period printed.


So free users were left with pictures of their screens unless a board link or copy-paste still works. That's why the comparison below asks every tool one question: can it turn a screenshot into a design you can edit?


Non-designers in design tools aren't a niche group.[Figma's IPO prospectus](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579878/000162828025037014/figma424b4.htm) , filed with the SEC in July 2025, says developers, PMs, marketers and other non-designers "made up two-thirds of our more than 13 million monthly active users" in the three months ended March 31, 2025.


That describes Figma's own users, not the whole market, but it shows how much design work happens outside design teams. If that's you, the[principles of design](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/what-every-non-designer-ought-to-know-the-principles-of-design) will do as much for your mockups as any tool switch.


## The best Visily alternatives


The last column asks the question that matters most after the shutdown: does the vendor document turning an uploaded screenshot into an editable design, and on which plan?


Awesomic brings AI agents and vetted experts into one app. Start with a prompt to build a website, app, campaign, deck or video, then switch models or bring in a vetted expert without losing the project context. AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


If your saved screens are images, the "Yes" rows are your shortlist.


### 1. Awesomic


**Best for:** Turning a rough idea into a working page


**Overview:** We'll start with what we don't do: Awesomic has no screenshot converter, sketch import, Visily import or wireframing canvas.


Instead of a static mockup, you describe the screen in plain words, our agents build it as a working page on your project's own cloud computer, and one click publishes it to a live link.


Our brand memory carries your brand, files and decisions from screen to screen, so screen five starts from the rules screen one set. When a draft needs a designer, our All-in-One plan, bought separately, matches you with a UI/UX designer among 200+ vetted experts across 30+ skill sets, and you hand the task over in the chat.


**Key features:**


- Parallel agents, one chat each, all working on the same project files.
- Projects you share by link, with your team, agents and experts in one chat.
- Connections to Notion, Slack and Figma, plus your own MCP servers.
- An iOS app for describing a change, watching the agent work and previewing the result.


**Pricing:** Light runs $19 a person a month, and that figure is also the person's monthly AI budget. Agentic plans bill monthly, aren't refundable, and unused budget resets each month.


For current Awesomic plans and capabilities, see[the pricing page](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


For one person on Light, that comes to $219 a month by our math, before any seat fees. All-in-One's $3,219 already includes a Light subscription, and the same math puts it at $3,419 or more with the fee; a second fee on the included Light isn't ruled out.


**Pros:** Clickable pages instead of static frames, a single click to publish them live, brand memory across screens, 200+ templates, a vetted UI/UX designer on a separate plan


**Cons:** AI-agent plans start at $19/month, and expert plans start at $1,799/month.[See current plans](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) .


**How to start using it:**


1. Go with Light, or with All-in-One if a designer should join from day one.
2. Read the checkout total.
3. Add your brand files and describe the first screen.
4. Click through the page and request changes in the chat.
5. Publish it and send the live link to whoever signs off.


**Why it's a good Visily alternative:** Stakeholders click through a real page instead of a picture of one, and because it looks finished, mark early versions as drafts.


**Final verdict:** To get Visily back as closely as possible, pick UX Pilot or a screenshot converter. Choose Awesomic when the mockup should become a working page, or when a designer should take it from there.


[Get started](https://www.awesomic.com/pricing) on Light to build your first screen.


### 2. UX Pilot


**Overview:** UX Pilot generates UI screens and wireframes from a prompt, and it's the only alternative we found with a documented way out of Visily. Its migration page offers three routes: "Import your .vis files, or use a board link or copy and paste if your board still opens, and every screen comes back editable in UX Pilot."


The same page says "UX Pilot copies your images when you import." It names no plan for the import beyond "Free to start", but if all you kept was a screenshot, reference image-to-design is included on every plan, Free among them.


**Key features:**


- Visily import from a .vis file, a board link or pasted screens.
- Autoflow for multi-screen flows.
- Predictive heatmaps and an AI design review to check a screen before you share it.


**Pricing:** The free plan gives you 80 credits a day and one project. Pro is $19 a month billed yearly, or $29 monthly, with 750 credits a month and export to Figma and code, while Teams costs $31 a user a month billed yearly, or $39 monthly.


**Pros:** A documented Visily file import, image-to-design on every plan, a free plan with daily credits


**Cons:** Figma and code export aren't on Free, free designs are for non-commercial use only, real-time collaboration starts on Teams


**Why it's a good Visily alternative:** It brings back the boards you saved as screens you can keep editing, so you skip the redraw.


**Final verdict:** Start with UX Pilot if you have .vis files or a board that still opens.


### 3. Mockflow


**Overview:** Mockflow pairs a whiteboard with WireframePro, its wireframing tool, and an AI helper called Mida. Its help docs describe what a Visily user needs: "Give Mida a photo of a whiteboard, a screenshot or handwritten notes and it rebuilds them on the board as editable diagrams, wireframes and plans."


That feature isn't on the free Basic plan. WireframePro's "Attach a screenshot or sketch" option also recreates a picture as an editable wireframe for AI credits, and the docs put it on Plus and Max too, so Mockflow's place here rests on Plus. Once a screen is rebuilt, you can restyle it in a click as Sketchy, Outline, Hi-fi or Blueprint.


**Key features:**


- Screenshot, sketch, photo or URL to an editable wireframe.
- One-click restyling between sketchy and high-fidelity looks.
- Meetings, chat and video comments on the board.


**Pricing:** Basic costs nothing for personal and nonprofit use, with 100 AI credits a month and 4 projects. Plus costs $9 an editor a month on yearly billing with 800 credits, Max $14 on the same terms with 2,000 credits plus Figma and code export, and Mockflow showed us no readable monthly price in dollars.


**Pros:** The lowest annual price among paid plans with screenshot conversion, whiteboard photos handled too, free viewers


**Cons:** Basic rules out commercial work, Figma and code export only on Max, a Basic account nobody signs in to for 60 days may be closed


**Where a whiteboard helps:** If your team sketched flows on a wall before opening Visily, Mockflow turns those photos into wireframes on the same board.


**Final verdict:** Choose Mockflow if your product ideas start on a whiteboard and a per-editor plan suits you.


### 4. Uizard


**Overview:** Uizard, now part of Miro (its logo reads "uizard miro LABS"), is a mockup tool with two scanners. Its Screenshot Scanner promises to "Turn screenshots of apps, features, or digital products into editable mockups in seconds", and a Wireframe Scanner does the same for hand-drawn sketches.


The scan quota is what separates the plans: 3 a month on Free, 500 on Pro and 5,000 on Business. Free is enough to test a couple of saved screens, not a whole project. For new screens, Autodesigner 2.0 on paid plans turns a text prompt into a full project.


**Key features:**


- Screenshot Scanner for app and website screenshots.
- Wireframe Scanner for paper sketches.
- Autodesigner 2.0 for text-to-project drafts, with React and CSS handoff on Pro.


**Pricing:** Free covers 2 projects of 5 screens each. Pro is $12 a month billed annually, or $19 monthly, and Business is $39 a month, billed annually only.


**Pros:** Screenshot conversion on every plan, sketch scanning as well, a low Pro price


**Cons:** Free allows 3 AI generations a month, Free exports at 1x only, Business is annual only


**Who gets the most from it:** A founder with a folder of saved Visily screens who wants editable mockups back without learning a design tool.


**Final verdict:** Pick Uizard if most of your Visily work survives as images and you'll scan more than three a month.


### 5. Banani


**Overview:** Banani is an AI UI generator with a dedicated screenshot feature: "Generate editable UI designs from your screenshots or images in seconds." Its FAQ confirms you can "upload screenshots of your existing product and edit them after conversion," which is the job a saved Visily export needs done.


From there, you can generate further screens from a text prompt, so one recovered screen can grow into a flow. Everything runs on credits. Free gives you 12 a month plus 3 a day, and generation pauses when you reach zero.


**Key features:**


- Screenshot or image to editable UI.
- Prompt-generated screens that extend a flow.
- HTML and CSS export, plus Figma export, on paid plans.


**Pricing:** Plus is $12 a month billed yearly, or $20 monthly, with 100 monthly and 10 daily credits. Pro lifts the credit limit for $30 a month billed yearly, or $50 monthly.


**Pros:** Screenshot conversion free to start, flows that grow from a single screen, a 40% saving on annual billing


**Cons:** Figma export is paid only, a small free credit allowance, generation stops when credits run out


**The case for it:** It turns a flat export into a screen you can edit and extend.


**Final verdict:** Choose Banani if you want to rebuild a whole flow from the one or two screens you managed to save.


### 6. Balsamiq


**Overview:** Balsamiq makes deliberately rough, low-fidelity wireframes, and its AI now converts images: "Drop in a screenshot of any app or website, and instantly turn it into an editable wireframe." It handles "whiteboard pics or napkin doodles" the same way.


The conversion works on every Cloud plan and costs about 16 credits a screen, so Starter's 500 AI credits per editor cover about 31 conversions, by our math. A finished wireframe turns into a clickable prototype in one click, at about 8 to 10 credits a screen.


**Key features:**


- Screenshot and sketch to editable wireframe.
- One-click wireframe to interactive prototype.
- An MCP server for Claude and Cursor.


**Pricing:** There's no free plan, only a 14-day trial with no card. Starter costs $16 an editor a month on annual billing, or $23 monthly, with room for 10 projects, while Teams is $24 billed annually, or $34 monthly, for 100 projects.


**Pros:** Conversion on every plan, a low-fi look that keeps feedback on layout, free reviewers


**Cons:** No free plan, exports only as PDF or image, a 10-project cap on Starter


**Why low fidelity is the point:** Rough screens keep stakeholders talking about structure instead of colors and fonts.


**Final verdict:** Choose Balsamiq if you liked Visily's low-fidelity mode and rarely switched to the polished one.


### 7. Excalidraw


**Overview:** Excalidraw is a hand-drawn-style whiteboard with live collaboration by link. It doesn't convert screenshots: its AI list covers "Text to diagram", "Wireframe to code" and "Mermaid to Excalidraw", so a saved Visily image becomes a reference you redraw on top of.


That's a fair trade if your screens were mostly boxes and arrows. The free plan gives you one infinite scene, unlimited collaborators and 10 AI requests a day, and Wireframe to code turns a wireframe you've sketched into code.


**Key features:**


- A hand-drawn canvas that a whole team can edit at once.
- Text to diagram for flows you'd rather describe than draw.
- PDF and PowerPoint export on Excalidraw+.


**Pricing:** The free plan exports PNG and SVG. Excalidraw+ is $6 a user a month billed annually, or $7 monthly, with a 14-day trial, unlimited scenes and 100 AI requests a day, and it takes card payments only.


**Pros:** The lowest paid price on this list, unlimited collaborators on Free, a sketch style that invites honest feedback


**Cons:** No screenshot conversion, no built-in UI kit for app screens (community libraries such as a Lo-Fi Wireframing Kit work on every plan), Free saves only one scene


**When a sketch is enough:** For a flow you only need to explain once in a meeting, a quick drawing does the job.


**Final verdict:** Pick Excalidraw if your Visily boards were mostly flows and boxes rather than finished-looking screens.


### 8. Moqups


**Overview:** Moqups puts wireframes, diagrams and whiteboards in one browser app. It can't convert an uploaded image, but its free Chrome and Firefox extension can "convert live webpages, parts of a page, or selected elements, into fully editable mockups." It can also bring AI-generated designs in as editable layouts.


For someone leaving Visily, that helps in one case: if a mockup was based on a live page, you can pull that page in and edit it. Moqups also imports Balsamiq files, though there's no AI screen generation inside the app itself.


**Key features:**


- A webpage-to-mockup browser extension.
- Wireframes, diagrams and whiteboards in one project.
- An MCP connection for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor on paid plans.


**Pricing:** Free gives one seat 2 projects of up to 400 objects each. Starter's regular price is $9 a month on an annual plan, or $12 billed monthly, which a promotion running at the time of writing cut to $7 or $11, and Business covers 3 seats for a regular $21 a month billed annually.


**Pros:** Live pages become editable mockups, Balsamiq file import, diagrams and screens side by side


**Cons:** No conversion from an image, live collaboration only from Business, a 400-object cap per project on Free


**Its edge for a migrating team:** A flowchart and the mockups it describes sit in one file.


**Final verdict:** Choose Moqups if your Visily boards mixed diagrams with screens and you can live without image conversion.


### 9. Whimsical


**Overview:** Whimsical is a workspace for flowcharts, wireframes, mind maps and docs. Its Agent "turns a text prompt into a wireframe on your board," and Whimsical's docs say the Agent accepts screenshots and mockups as context to build from, but Whimsical advertises no screenshot-to-wireframe conversion, so we counted it as a "No".


AI here runs on credits. Every account gets 10 to try, and they don't renew; after that, credits cost $0.10 each in bundles of 250, 1,000 or 10,000 and expire after a year. Wireframes come out low-fidelity.


**Key features:**


- Wireframes next to the flowcharts and docs that explain them.
- Whimsical Agent for prompt-to-wireframe drafts.
- An MCP server.


**Pricing:** Free allows 50 board objects and 50 doc blocks a month, with a watermark on exports. Pro costs $10 an editor each month on yearly billing, or $12 monthly, and Business costs $20 yearly, or $24 monthly.


**Pros:** Flows, wireframes and docs in one place, a text-to-wireframe agent, a low Pro price


**Cons:** No advertised screenshot conversion, 10 one-time AI credits before you pay per credit, no dedicated mobile app


**Where it fits after Visily:** Teams that used Visily's diagram generator as much as its screens get both on one board.


**Final verdict:** Choose Whimsical if the written spec around your screens matters as much as the screens.


### 10. Wireframe.cc


**Overview:** Wireframe.cc is the simplest tool on this list, and it has no AI anywhere. You draw a rectangle and pick what it should be, while a limited palette keeps every screen at wireframe fidelity.


The free version needs no account. You get a public, single-page wireframe, and each save gets its own public URL. Premium plans add clickable multi-page wireframes and PDF and PNG export, and every Premium plan carries every feature.


**Key features:**


- A draw-a-box editor with very little to learn.
- A fixed palette that keeps screens at wireframe fidelity.
- Clickable multi-page wireframes on Premium.


**Pricing:** Solo costs $12 a month on annual billing, or $19 month to month, for one user, and Trio costs $33 a month on annual billing, or $39 month to month, for three. Taxes are added at checkout.


**Pros:** No account needed to start, almost no learning curve, every feature on every Premium plan


**Cons:** No AI or screenshot conversion, free wireframes are public, no real-time collaboration documented


**Who should pick it:** Someone who wants to sketch one screen quickly and send a link to it.


**Final verdict:** Choose Wireframe.cc if Visily's AI was always more than you needed.


## Getting your old screens back


Here's what to feed each tool, what comes back and the plan you need:


Whatever you saved decides your shortlist: a .vis file points to UX Pilot, and a folder of PNGs points to the four converters after it.


Even a clean import is only a starting point. In a small r/FigmaDesign thread,[one user moving Visily wireframes](https://www.reddit.com/r/FigmaDesign/comments/1lujoo8/visily_to_figma/) into Figma found the developer still needed iOS-specific screens, and a reply put it bluntly: "Most imports no matter the software results in having to redo a load of the work again." It's one Reddit thread, so treat it as anecdote, but plan for some redrawing.


Once the screens are back, linking them into a clickable flow is the next job, which is where[prototyping tools](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/prototyping-tools) come in.


## How to choose as a non-designer


Start with what you saved, then match the tool to how your team works:


- If you saved .vis files, or a board still opens, go to UX Pilot first.
- If you have images and want polished screens back, try Uizard or Banani on their free plans.
- If you'd rather stay rough on purpose, use Balsamiq or Wireframe.cc.
- If your ideas start on a whiteboard, look at Mockflow Plus or Excalidraw.
- If your boards mixed diagrams with screens, compare Moqups and Whimsical.


Whichever you pick, make several rough versions before you polish one. In a 2010 study published in ACM TOCHI,[Dow and colleagues at Stanford](https://hci.stanford.edu/publications/2010/parallel-prototyping/ParallelPrototyping2010.pdf) had 33 participants design web banner ads either in parallel or one after another, and "ads created in the Parallel condition significantly outperformed those from the Serial condition."


The two best click-through rates, 735 and 578 clicks per million impressions, came from parallel ads, and the two worst, both serial, got no clicks. It's a small study of ad design, not app screens, but the lesson likely carries over: screenshot conversion and AI drafts make a second and third version cheap.


Polish has a cost too. In an r/ProductManagement thread on[practicing wireframing](https://www.reddit.com/r/ProductManagement/comments/1x3cm84/how_to_practice_wireframing/) , the top reply said a wireframe's job is to settle the hierarchy of information, and one commenter who vibe-coded a wireframe said it looked "deceptively far along" and worried it would lock the team into a structure too soon. That's one Reddit discussion, but it's a reason to label early drafts as drafts.


Several versions are only comparable if they answer the same question, so agree on what the screens are for before anyone opens a tool.[A short creative brief](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/crafting-a-good-creative-brief-unlock-business-results-faster) does that in a page.


## Visily competitors we left out


A few came close. Google Stitch can generate UI from a screenshot, but Google publishes no price for it. Miro Prototypes converts a screenshot into an editable prototype on Miro's Business plan or on Enterprise with the Accelerate license, and since Miro also owns Uizard, we kept one of the two.


Claritee lets you paste screenshots onto its canvas, which isn't conversion, and Motiff, still on some older lists, has been discontinued. Designers who work in Figma every day need plugins and design-system support, which our[UX Pilot alternatives](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ux-pilot-alternatives) list covers.


## Your first week without Visily


Save first and choose second. Before November 30, sign in if you still can and export or screenshot every board. This week, run your three most important screens through two tools from different groups, say UX Pilot and Uizard, and time how long each takes to reach a screen you'd show a stakeholder.


Keep the tool that needed the least fixing. If that mockup is really the start of a product, Awesomic lets you[hire a product designer](https://www.awesomic.com/hire/hire-a-product-designer) to carry it forward.


## FAQ


### When will Visily delete my data?


On November 30, 2026, according to Visily's shutdown post, which calls the deletion permanent. Visily's shutdown date was October 31, and visily.ai now sends almost every page to a login screen with no sign-up option.


### Can I still export my Visily designs?


We can't confirm it, because we had no account to test with. Before the shutdown, paid workspaces could export to Figma as a .vis file, to code, or as high-resolution images without a watermark, while free accounts got watermarked 1x JPG, PNG or PDF files. Visily's shutdown post says all designs can be exported, including to Figma, but with no account we couldn't test that. If you can sign in, try exporting first and screenshot whatever fails.


### Which tool imports Visily files?


Among the alternatives here, UX Pilot is the only one we found that documents it. It takes .vis files, a board link or pasted screens, though images from a .vis import done after the deletion date might not load, and no plan is named for the import.


Visily's own help also documents importing .vis files into Figma through Visily's Figma plugin, but we can't say whether that route still works after the shutdown.


### Is there a free Visily alternative that converts screenshots?


Yes, three. UX Pilot's free plan includes image-to-design with 80 credits a day (its Terms limit free designs to non-commercial use), Uizard's Free plan scans 3 screenshots a month, and Banani's free plan gives you 12 monthly and 3 daily credits to spend, screenshot conversion included. Mockflow's conversion starts on Plus, and Balsamiq has no free plan, only a 14-day trial.


### Which Visily alternative is easiest for a non-designer?


Wireframe.cc has the least to learn: you draw a box, pick what it is, and need no account. For editable screens from old images, Uizard and Banani both start free. Most[UX design tools](https://www.awesomic.com/blog/ux-design-tools) assume a designer is at the keyboard, so try two of these on one real screen before you pay.
